Build templates that work well with Copilot

Applies to: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365.

Last Updated: Oct 2026

A Brand Kit stores the logos, templates, fonts, and colors that keep presentations on brand. When you add a PowerPoint template to a Brand Kit, Copilot checks it and tells you how well it’s set up to be used as a source for generated presentations.

Copilot builds presentations by reading your template’s slide masters, layouts, theme, placeholders, and sample slides. The more clearly those are defined, the more consistent and on-brand the results. The template check shows you what’s working, what to improve, and how—so you can fix things once, in the template, instead of correcting generated decks over and over.

Important

The check never changes your file, and it never blocks you from saving. It gives you recommendations; you decide what to act on and when.

Assess your template

Template assessment runs automatically when you upload a new template to the Brand Kit. You can also run the assessment at any time on existing templates.

Assess a new template when you upload it
  • In your Brand Kit, select Templates, and then select Add template.
  • Choose your PowerPoint file. The Save as brand template window opens.
  • Under Template assessment, the status appears while Copilot works: Checking your template for compatibility…
  • You can keep filling in the template name, tags, and description while the assessment runs.
  • When the assessment finishes, review the results, and then select Add to Brand Kit.
Assess an existing template
  • In your Brand Kit, select Templates.
  • Point to the template you want to assess, select More options (…), and then select Template assessment.
  • Wait for Checking your template for compatibility… to finish. When it’s done, you’ll see one of these:
  • Result
  • What it means
  • Check complete. Your template’s ready to use with Copilot.
  • Nothing needs attention.
  • Check complete. We have suggestions for your template.
  • There are recommendations to review.
  • We couldn’t check this template. Try again.
  • The assessment didn’t run. Try again.
  • Select View suggestions to see the details.

Read your results

At the top of the results, a message summarizes the outcome.

Message

What to do

Looks good! Your template’s ready to use with Copilot.

Nothing to do.

Your template could work better with Copilot. Here are our recommendations.

Review the recommendations below. You can save the template now and improve it later.

Copilot can’t use this file type. Save the template as a supported PowerPoint file to continue.

Save the file as .pptx or .potx and add it again.

Copilot couldn’t read part of this template. Repair it or restore a working copy to continue.

Repair the file in PowerPoint, or go back to a working copy.

Below the message, each recommendation appears as a row. The row itself states what was found, so you can scan the list without expanding anything. Each row has a label that shows its status and the part of the template it applies to—for example, Suggestion · Theme or Suggestion · Sample slides.

  • Suggestion — the template works, but Copilot produces better output if you make the change.
  • Pass — this part of your template is already set up well. Select View Passed Items to see them. Some issues, like an unsupported file type or a file Copilot can’t read, must be fixed before Copilot can use the template. Only the template file, slide master, and theme checks can reach this state.

Expand a row to see Why it matters and How to improve. For sample-slide checks, Found on lists the slides where the issue appears.

To share the results with whoever maintains the template, select Copy results. When you’re finished, select Done.

Note

The check only reports what it actually observed. It won’t tell you something is missing just because it couldn’t be measured.

What Copilot checks

Template file

Status

What the result says

Pass

This is a PowerPoint file Copilot can use.

Must fix

Copilot can’t use this file type.

Suggestion

Some design details may be missing because this template was last saved in PowerPoint for the web.

Why it matters: Copilot can’t use the template unless the file is in a supported and readable PowerPoint format. And because Copilot reads the saved template package, the file needs to include its full design.

How to improve:

  • Must fix — Open the template in PowerPoint and save it as .pptx or .potx. Macro-enabled, password-protected, and older .ppt files aren’t supported.
  • Suggestion — Open the template in PowerPoint for Windows or Mac and save it again to include the full design.
Slide master

Status

What the result says

Pass

Copilot can read every part of this template.

Must fix

Some parts of this template couldn’t be read.

Suggestion

Some slide parts of this template didn’t load correctly.

Why it matters: Copilot builds slides from the template’s masters and layouts, so those parts need to be present and readable.

How to improve:

  • Must fix — Open the template in PowerPoint and use Repair if it’s offered. Otherwise, restore a working copy.
  • Suggestion — Open the template in PowerPoint and save a fresh copy to rebuild its internal structure.
Theme

Two checks look at your theme.

Your theme definition

Status

What the result says

Pass

Your template has a complete, consistent set of theme colors and fonts.

Must fix

Your template is missing theme colors, theme fonts, or both.

Suggestion

Some slide masters or layouts use different theme colors or fonts.

Why it matters: Copilot styles generated slides from the theme. A complete, consistent theme helps keep new slides on brand.

How to improve:

  • Must fix — In Slide Master, open Colors and choose a full palette. Then open Fonts and set Heading and Body fonts.
  • Suggestion — In Slide Master, apply the same theme colors and fonts to every master and layout you keep. How your text uses the theme

Status

What the result says

Pass

Your text uses the template’s theme fonts and colors.

Suggestion

Some text uses fonts or colors that aren’t part of your theme.

Why it matters: Text that uses theme fonts and colors can update if you change your theme. Custom formatting might not update.

How to improve: In Slide Master, use Theme Fonts and Theme Colors for text placeholders. Apply them to text on sample slides, too.

Placeholders

Status

What the result says

Pass

Your content is in placeholders Copilot can fill.

Suggestion

Some sample content is in text boxes, not placeholders Copilot can fill.

Why it matters: Copilot puts generated content into layout placeholders, so text in loose text boxes has nowhere to land.

How to improve: In Slide Master, replace text boxes used for main content with placeholders. Choose Picture, Chart, Table, or SmartArt when the content type is fixed.

Sample slides

Sample slides are the finished example slides in your template. They show Copilot how your team actually uses your design. Several checks look at them.

Range of examples

Status

What the result says

Pass

Your sample slides show Copilot a good range of content.

Suggestion

Add sample slides with varied layouts and examples of text, images, and data.

If your template has none: Your template has no sample slides.

Why it matters: Sample slides show Copilot how your team combines text, images, and data in your designs.

How to improve: Add sample slides with real content that covers text, images, and data. Vary the layouts and avoid exact copies.

Completed examples

Status

What the result says

Pass

Your sample slides show examples in the content areas meant to demonstrate the layout.

Suggestion

Some sample slides don’t show examples in all content areas.

Why it matters: Sample slides show Copilot what belongs in each area; an empty area in a sample doesn’t provide an example. This is about your sample slides, not about blank placeholders in your layouts.

How to improve: Add example content to the areas meant to demonstrate the layout. Leave areas intentionally blank when they don’t need an example.

Text that fits

Status

What the result says

Pass

Your sample text fits its placeholders.

Suggestion

Some text overflows its placeholder.

Why it matters: Text that fits its placeholder gives Copilot an example it can reproduce without overflow.

How to improve: Shorten the text or enlarge the placeholder in Slide Master. Copilot doesn’t resize text, so overflow can carry into new slides.

Editable content

Status

What the result says

Pass

Your examples use editable PowerPoint content.

Suggestion

Some sample-slide content is embedded or locked, so Copilot can’t update it.

Why it matters: Copilot can restyle and refill native PowerPoint shapes, tables, and charts, but not embedded objects, or shapes, text boxes, or other objects that have been grouped together and locked.

How to improve: Replace embedded objects and pictures of tables or charts with editable PowerPoint tables or charts. To make a locked group editable, select the group and unlock it.

Speaker notes

Status

What the result says

Pass

Your sample slides have speaker notes.

Suggestion

Some sample slides don’t have speaker notes.

If none have notes: None of your sample slides have speaker notes.

Why it matters: Speaker notes tell Copilot what a sample slide is for and when to use it. These notes can guide Copilot even if they aren’t meant for presentation viewers.

How to improve: In the Notes pane, describe what each sample slide is for and when Copilot should use it. The notes are for Copilot; they don’t have to be written for your audience.

Tip

Speaker notes do double duty. Beyond helping Copilot pick the right sample slide, you can use them to steer how Copilot treats a slide—for example, “Always include this cover slide.” See Manage template settings in your Brand Kit for Copilot in PowerPoint.

Fix your template with Copilot in PowerPoint

You can ask Copilot in PowerPoint to apply the recommendations for you.

  • In Template assessment, select Copy results.
  • Open your template in PowerPoint, and then open Copilot.
  • Enter the following prompt, paste the results after it, and then send:
  • Fix the template issues from the checker report, keeping the existing design and slide count:
  • Copilot might ask how you want to act on the report. Choose an option, and then select Confirm:
    • Fix the existing slides — fixes theme, placeholder, and text-fit issues and keeps your current design and slide count.
    • Fix and expand examples — applies the fixes and adds sample slides where your examples have gaps.
    • Explain the report first — explains the recommendations without changing your template.
  • Review the changes. Copilot summarizes what it updated and flags anything that still needs your attention.
  • Save the template, upload it to your Brand Kit, and run the assessment again to confirm the fixes. Tip

Copilot fixes the template structure, not your content. If it flags issues like inconsistent sample data, review those slides yourself.

Improve your template and assess again

  • Open the template in PowerPoint and make the changes described under How to improve.
  • Save the template and upload the updated version to your Brand Kit. The assessment runs automatically, so you can confirm your changes worked. You can also run the assessment on an existing template at any time—for example, after someone else updates it, or to re-check a template you haven’t looked at in a while.

Tip

Make theme and placeholder changes in the slide master and layouts rather than on individual slides. Changes at the master level apply everywhere the layout is used and won’t reappear the next time your template is updated.

Tip

If you only have time for one thing, add sample slides. They’re the clearest signal Copilot has about how your design is meant to be used.

Quick reference

  • Upload your template to your Brand Kit, or select More options (…) > Template assessment on an existing template.
  • Wait for Checking your template for compatibility… to finish.
  • Select View suggestions.
  • Resolve anything that must be fixed, then work through the suggestions.
  • Expand a row to see Why it matters and How to improve.
  • Fix the template in PowerPoint yourself, or select Copy results and ask Copilot in PowerPoint to fix it.
  • Upload the updated version and assess it again to confirm your changes.

Microsoft Copilot help & learning

Copilot in PowerPoint image suggestions FAQ

Applies to: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365, Microsoft 365.

Last reviewed June 2026

Copilot in PowerPoint can suggest or generate images, and you can learn more about them in the following frequently asked questions.

Are the images provided by Copilot AI-generated?

AI powers image searches based on your prompt in Copilot. See Add a slide or image to your presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint to learn how to try it for yourself.

It depends on how you added the image. You can ask Copilot to add a stock image for you, in which case Microsoft utilizes a licensed stock library to provide royalty free images, icons, and illustrations through Copilot. Or you can ask it to use DALL·E to generate an image for you based on the prompt you enter.

What am I allowed to use these images for?

You can use any image, icon, or illustration suggested by Copilot within a Microsoft 365 or Microsoft Office app or service for anything permitted by your applicable Microsoft 365 or Office license. Review your End-User License Agreement (EULA) to understand exactly what you can do with your Microsoft 365 or Office license.

As with other stock images, icons, and illustrations provided by Microsoft 365 and Office apps, you can use the creative content as you like within an Office or Microsoft 365 app. For commercial customers, this includes selling PowerPoint presentations, Excel workbooks, or Word documents that include this content, just as you would have sold these files in the past.

This includes exporting the Microsoft 365 file to another format. You can modify the picture, use it in the file forever, and use it anywhere in the world. Basically, do the same things that you would have done with Microsoft 365 documents in the past, but now you can include the stock images, icons, and illustrations suggested by Copilot.

You don’t own a license to the Microsoft 365 images for general use, so you can’t take the images outside of Microsoft 365 or Office and use them in a different context. Copy-pasting into something other than Microsoft 365, or selecting the pictures and using Save as from the right-click context menu, are common examples of actions that take the pictures outside of Microsoft 365.

What are generated images?

Designer’s Image Creator has been made available in Microsoft Copilot to help users easily generate images for their slides and documents. Generated images are created with DALL·E 3, an AI model that can create images from text inputs. Given a prompt, Copilot can generate a set of images matching that prompt.

Tips for prompting generated images?

Creating an image works differently than searching for stock images.

Asking Copilot to “add a stock image” will add a stock image to your presentation. Asking Copilot to “generate an image” will use Dall-E 3 to create a generated image to add to your presentation.

Designer’s Image Creator works best when you’re more descriptive, so get creative and add details like adjectives, locations, or even artistic styles such as ‘digital art’ and ‘photorealistic.’

Here’s an example of a how to create a longer, more descriptive prompt:

  • Original prompt: “astronaut”
  • Descriptive prompt: “A close-up photo of an astronaut in a glowing suit made of plasma, as if the galaxy is inside of it, putting on their helmet, but you can’t see their face because of the visor, realistic, film stock, bright colors.⁠”

How were generated images in Copilot evaluated?

Designer’s Image Creator in Copilot was evaluated through extensive manual and automatic testing. More evaluation was performed over custom datasets for offensive and malicious prompts and responses. In addition, Designer’s Image Creator is continuously evaluated with user feedback.

What are the limitations of generated images in Copilot?

Generated images are available to Copilot Pro users only, and not yet available to Commercial Microsoft Copilot users.

Designer’s Image Creator has controls in place to prevent the generation of harmful images in accordance with our content policy. When our system detects that a potentially harmful image could be generated by a prompt, it automatically blocks the prompt and informs the user. Additionally, when our system detects a potentially harmful generated image, it automatically blocks this image from the set of images delivered to the user.

What operational factors and settings allow for effective and responsible use of generated images in Copilot?

Designer’s Image Creator has been reviewed by our Responsible AI (RAI) team. We follow Microsoft’s RAI principals and have implemented:

  • Responsible AI handling pipeline to mitigate the risks like harmful, inappropriate content.
  • In-product user feedback with which users can report offensive content back to Microsoft. We help make it clear that Image Creator’s images are generated by AI. We have implemented content credentials, provenance based on the C2PA standard, to help users identify AI generated Images.

We allow living artists, celebrities, and organizations to make requests to limit the creation of images associated with their names and brands via the AI-powered features option on our Report a Concern form.

Create a new presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint

Applies to: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365, PowerPoint for iPad.

Note

If you don’t see Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or OneNote, it might not be included with your Microsoft 365 subscription or available based on your organization’s settings. Learn which Copilot license you have.

Last updated: October 2026

  • Start a new presentation in PowerPoint.
  • Open Copilot Chat using the Copilot icon at the bottom-right corner of the screen.
  • If you want, choose an AI model from the model selector, or leave it set to Auto.
  • If your organization requires a Brand Kit, in Select brand, choose the Brand Kit you want Copilot to use for the presentation. If you’re a consumer, your organization doesn’t require a Brand Kit, or your organization hasn’t created one yet, you can skip this step.
  • If you selected a Brand Kit, you’ll see it attached to the prompt box.
  • If you need to create or update a Brand Kit first, select Manage kits, add or update brand assets such as logos, templates, fonts, colors, images, icons, brand voice, style, and skills, then select Publish Brand Kit to make it available in Copilot. See Create and manage official Brand Kits in Microsoft Copilot for details.
  • In the prompt box, describe the presentation you want Copilot to create. For examples, see Edit with Copilot in PowerPoint.
  • Copilot may ask clarifying questions, such as who the audience is, how long the deck should be, which template or design direction to use, and what kind of imagery to include. Answer the questions or skip them and let Copilot decide.
  • Copilot will gather context, generate content, and use your selected template to create the presentation. If you selected a Brand Kit, Copilot also applies it.

Best practices when creating a presentation from a Word document

Leverage Word Styles to help Copilot understand the structure of your document

By using Styles in Word to organize your document, Copilot will better understand your source document structure and how to break it up into slides of a presentation.

Include images that are relevant to your presentation

When creating a presentation, Copilot will try to incorporate any images found in your Word document.

Start with your organization’s template

If your organization uses a standard presentation template, start with this file before creating a presentation with Copilot. Starting with a template will let Copilot know that you’d like to retain the presentation’s theme and design. Copilot will use existing layouts to build a presentation for you. Learn more about making your presentations look great with Copilot in PowerPoint.

Tip

Copilot works best with Word documents that are smaller than 24 MB.

Create interactive slides with Copilot in PowerPoint

Applies to: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365, PowerPoint for iPad.

Note

If you don’t see Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or OneNote, it might not be included with your Microsoft 365 subscription or available based on your organization’s settings. Learn which Copilot license you have.

Interactive slides in PowerPoint are slides created by Copilot with visual interactivity that you and your audience can explore together. Describe the story you want to tell, and Copilot builds a slide you can click through, revealing context, steps, or data points as you interact with it.

Create an interactive slide

Select Interactive Slide from the PowerPoint Home or Insert ribbon to get started in the Copilot chat pane, then tell Copilot what you want to create. You can start with one of the suggested categories or choose to create a custom interactive slide. Be specific about the type of slide you want, and Copilot can match the content to your narrative.

You can also find Create interactive slide in the Copilot skill picker in PowerPoint.

Ground your slide in your own content

Interactive slides can be based on content you already have by using Work IQ. Ask Copilot to build a dashboard based on a snapshot of data from an Excel workbook, or a timeline from a project document, and it uses your work content to fill in the numbers and dates.

Refine your slide

Not quite right? Keep the Copilot pane open and keep prompting — “Make this a bar chart,” “Add a filter by region,” or “Match the colors to my theme.” Copilot updates the slide for you.

Important

Interactive slides are created and updated through Copilot rather than by editing the slide directly, so send your changes as a prompt instead of reaching for the canvas.

Note

Interactive slides are optimized for a full slide experience. On Mac and iPad, other content on the slide appears behind the interactive content.

Present and share

When you present your deck with PowerPoint for Windows, Mac, web, or iPad, you can engage with the interactive slide to let the story unfold — expand a step, filter a chart, or move through a timeline, based on the slide that was created.

With PowerPoint for Windows, web, and iPad, interactive slides work with both presenter view and slide show. On Mac, you can interact with the slide in slide show view but not in presenter view. Support for interaction in presenter view on Mac is planned as a future improvement.

In PowerPoint Live in Microsoft Teams, each meeting attendee can interact independently with slides created using the Create interactive slide skill. Interactions aren’t shared; attendees see their own interactions, but not the presenter’s or other attendees’ interactions. Support for synchronizing presenter interactions across the meeting is planned as a future improvement.

Anyone you share the presentation with can explore the interactivity, even without a Copilot license.

What you need

License

Interactive slides are available to eligible consumer and commercial users who already have access to Copilot in PowerPoint, including Microsoft 365 Copilot Basic and Premium. There’s no separate license for interactive slides.

Supported versions

Rollout of the skill and ribbon button for PowerPoint for Windows and Mac for Current Channel and Monthly Enterprise Channel starts in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by end of October 2026. Users with access to Frontier, Microsoft 365 Insiders Beta Channel, or Current Channel (Preview) can use the skill now.

Rollout of the skill and ribbon button for PowerPoint for the web starts in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by end of October 2026. Users with access to Frontier can use the skill now.

For the best experience viewing and interacting with interactive slides, users should update to the latest Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise Channel releases for PowerPoint for Windows and Mac, latest App Store release for iPad, and for PowerPoint Live, the latest generally available versions of Microsoft Teams.

Where you can use interactive slides

  • Create or update: use the skill in the Copilot app and Copilot in PowerPoint for Windows, Mac, and web.
  • Interactivity is supported when viewing the slide in the Copilot app, PowerPoint for Windows, Mac, web, and iPad, and PowerPoint Live in Microsoft Teams.
  • No interactivity: iPhone, Android, and when printing and exporting to other formats like PDF. The slide appears as a non-interactive image of the slide content.

Accessibility

When presenting an interactive slide, left and right arrow keys always move between slides, even while an interactive slide is on screen. These keyboard commands for slide navigation aren’t captured by the slide’s interactive content, so you can always move forward or back across slides as needed.

To access the interactive content with a keyboard, press Tab to move focus into the interactive content, then Tab again to move through its elements in focus order. Each element shows a visible focus indicator.

Press Tab past the last element, or press Esc, to move focus back to PowerPoint. Press Esc again to leave the slide show.

Focus never moves into the interactive content on its own, so you can show a slide without changing what’s on it.

Note

Additional keyboard navigation optimizations are planned as a future improvement. Moving focus out of an interactive slide, and reaching the interactive slide toolbar with the keyboard, might work differently in PowerPoint for Mac and PowerPoint for the web.

Keep in mind

Copilot uses AI models to generate the layout, content, and behavior of your interactive slide. Like other AI-generated content, it might produce something you didn’t expect, and it might contain inaccuracies. Be sure to review and verify the information before you present or share.

We want to hear from you!

If there’s something you like about interactive slides — or if there’s something you don’t — send us feedback. Just select the thumbs up or thumbs down button underneath the Copilot chat box. Your feedback helps us improve the experience in PowerPoint.

Frequently asked questions

Where can I create or interact with interactive slides?

Create interactive slides with the Copilot app and with Copilot in PowerPoint for Windows, Mac, and web. You can interact with the slides in the Copilot app, PowerPoint for Windows, Mac, web, and iPad, and when presenting in PowerPoint Live in Teams. On iPhone and Android, interactive slides appear as a non-interactive image.

Can I edit interactive slides directly, without Copilot?

You can create or update interactive slides with the Copilot skill, but not directly by editing the slide. Copilot creates or updates the content for you.

Are interactive slides HTML pages?

Interactive slides create web views to display and provide interaction on your slide. The web views are sandboxed and do not connect to other content or services.

How can I reset an interactive slide to look like it did before I explored the interactions?

When you open a presentation file, interactive slides default to the starting layout based on when you created or last updated the slide with Copilot. As you interact, the slide might reflect your most recent interactions until you close the file.

Can I print an interactive slide or export it to PDF?

When a presentation with an interactive slide is printed or exported, the interactive slide appears as a non-interactive image of the slide content.

How do interactive slides work with Microsoft Purview organizational policies and Information Protection sensitivity labels?

The Create interactive slide skill uses Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot agents to create or update slides. To learn more, see Microsoft Purview data security and compliance protections for generative AI apps and Use Microsoft Purview to manage data security and compliance for AI agents.

Are there admin controls for interactive slides?

No. All users with the appropriate Copilot license can use the skill to create or update interactive slides. When you share a presentation with interactive slides, others can explore the interaction without a Copilot license.

Deploy organization skills for Copilot in PowerPoint

Applies to: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365, PowerPoint for iPad.

Note

If you don’t see Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or OneNote, it might not be included with your Microsoft 365 subscription or available based on your organization’s settings. Learn which Copilot license you have.

Microsoft 365 administrators can upload and deploy custom skills for use with Copilot in PowerPoint. You can make a skill available to everyone in your organization or to specific users and groups.

Upload and deploy a custom skill for your organization

  • Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • In the left navigation pane, select Agents > All agents. Select the More actions (…) menu, and then select Add agent.
  • On the Upload agent to publish page, select Choose file, and then upload the skill package (.zip).
  • Review the validation results. If validation fails, correct the package structure or manifest, and then upload the package again. For requirements, see Package a custom skill for deployment later in this article.
  • Choose who can use the skill. Select all users or specific users and groups, configure the available deployment options, and then complete the publishing flow.
  • To verify the deployment, go to Agents > Tools in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Select the skill to review its details, users, version, and deployment status.
  • After the skill is published and installed, open PowerPoint with an account included in the deployment. Open the Copilot chat pane, select the + menu in the prompt box, and then select Choose skills.
  • Find the custom skill shared by your organization in the skills list. The skill is visible only to users included in the deployment.

Package a custom skill for deployment

A custom skill ready to be deployed must be packaged as a .zip file that includes the skill files, an app manifest, and icons. The Microsoft 365 admin center validates the package when you upload it.

Before you upload the package, verify that it uses the following structure.

The manifest.json file describes the package to the Microsoft 365 admin center. For the latest manifest schema guidance, see Microsoft 365 app manifest schema reference.

Use a unique ID (in the form of a GUID) for the id property, provide concise names and descriptions, and make sure the paths match the files in the package. The following example shows a basic manifest.

{
  "$schema": "[developer.microsoft.com](https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/teams/v1.30/MicrosoftTeams.schema.json)",
  "manifestVersion": "1.30",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "id": "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "developer": {
    "name": "Rolly Seth",
    "websiteUrl": "https://localhost",
    "privacyUrl": "https://localhost/privacy",
    "termsOfUseUrl": "https://localhost/terms"
  },
  "name": {
    "short": "Infographic Summary",
    "full": "Presentation Infographic Summary"
  },
  "description": {
    "short": "Creates an infographic overview of a presentation.",
    "full": "Reads a presentation and generates an editorial-style infographic summary."
  },
  "icons": {
    "color": "color.png",
    "outline": "outline.png"
  },
  "accentColor": "#2E86DE",
  "agentSkills": [
    {
      "folder": "./skills/infographic-summary"
    }
  ]
}

Include both icon files referenced by manifest.json: a color.png icon and an outline.png icon. For icon requirements, see icon design requirements. The icons identify the skill in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

You can also use the Agent 365 CLI to prepare and publish a package, or to retrieve values required by the manifest, such as the agent blueprint ID. For more information, see Publish Agent to Microsoft Admin Center and Agent 365 CLI setup command reference.

Edit with Copilot in PowerPoint

Applies to: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365.

Last Updated: Oct 2026

Important

Copilot, including Brand Kit, is available in PowerPoint for Windows, Mac, and the web.

Copilot is an AI-powered assistant available in PowerPoint for Windows, Mac, and the web. It can be accessed by opening Copilot Chat using the Copilot icon at the bottom-right corner of the screen. It is on by default in the prompt box.

Copilot helps you create, edit, and understand your presentations. It understands document context, can perform multi-step tasks, and generates or edits content directly within PowerPoint, including:

  • Create Interactive Slides - Generate engaging interactive slides like dashboards, timelines, and summaries that people can explore with you, so your presentation feels like a story you’re walking through together.
  • Slide Editing and Structuring: Add new slides, update existing content, reorganize sections, and enhance overall flow with AI-assisted suggestions.
  • Image Generation and Enhancement: Use AI to create custom visuals or replace existing ones, with results inserted directly into your slides or shared in chat.
  • Presentation Understanding: Quickly summarize your deck, get answers to specific questions, and receive insights to help you better communicate your message. You can choose between different AI models, including Claude from Anthropic and ChatGPT from OpenAI, to power your Copilot experience when making changes directly in your presentation.

Copilot will work to understand and follow your presentation’s design and brand. A key way to help Copilot better understand your brand requirements is to populate a Brand Kit (available for enterprise users) with your brand assets.

The experience is designed to streamline presentation creation workflows and improve productivity. It has been designed with responsible AI in mind.

Try it now

Ready to try it out? You can use Copilot to create on-brand presentations and streamline a wide range of tasks.

  • Open PowerPoint.
  • Open Copilot Chat using the Copilot icon at the bottom-right corner of the screen and try these prompts:
  • Use current work content: “Add a slide with a chart showing our latest sales projections based on the spreadsheet in my files /link to the grounding doc and Teams meetings, and summarize the top three takeaways from the data underneath the chart.”
  • Improve presentation visuals: “Replace the bullet list on this slide with a detailed SmartArt timeline.”
  • Improve presentation visuals: “Make the image on this slide photorealistic.”
  • Complex reasoning and audience adaptation: “Update slides 4-6 for a UK audience.”

Set up your Brand Kit and template (for enterprise users)

To set up your Brand Kit and optimize your template for Copilot, please refer to the following articles. Note that you must have a Microsoft Copilot license to access Brand Kit.

  • Create and manage official Brand Kits in Microsoft Copilot

  • Keep your presentation on-brand with Copilot If you have set up a Brand Kit, select your Brand Kit in the Copilot Chat prompt box in PowerPoint and try the following:

  • Ask Copilot to create a branded presentation - Attach your Brand Kit to your prompt box and ask Copilot to “Build a 12-slide business review for my leadership team covering market trends, competitive landscape, our current position, key wins, open risks, and the next-quarter plan.”

  • Ask it to reformat your presentation to match the branded template style, applying consistent colors, fonts, and layouts throughout - such as “Restyle this slide to match the rest of the deck. Improve the layout and visual hierarchy, and use one of my branded images instead of the placeholder graphic.”

  • Edit your visuals to suit your unique use cases by asking Copilot to “Edit this image so it includes an object/person interacting with the product/background, keeping the same scenery, lighting, and color treatment so it still matches our brand look and feel.”

Improve your presentations with skills for Copilot in PowerPoint

Copilot in PowerPoint now includes built-in skills — ready-to-use commands that take action on your deck in a single click. Instead of crafting a long prompt, just pick a skill and let Copilot do the work, helping you improve storytelling and visual consistency faster, right alongside your existing Copilot workflows.

Copilot in PowerPoint skills
  • Review this presentation — Get detailed, slide-by-slide suggestions to strengthen structure, clarity, and storytelling. Copilot looks across your existing content and recommends edits to make your message land.
  • Visualize this slide — Transform a text-heavy slide into a polished, professional visual. Copilot turns your written content into an engaging image that elevates the look and feel of your deck.
  • Prepare for Questions — Analyze presentations to identify potential weak points and anticipate audience questions, helping users improve storytelling and deliver presentations more effectively.
How to use a skill
  • Open the Copilot Chat using the Copilot icon at the bottom-right corner of the screen.
  • Select the Skills menu.
  • Choose the skill (e.g. Review this presentation) and let Copilot help you (e.g. generate suggestions you can review and apply).

Frequently asked questions

What are the limitations of Copilot in PowerPoint? How can users limit the impacts of those limitations when using the system?

Limitations:

  • Large or complex presentations may exceed system limits. How to limit impacts:

  • Use the thumbs-down button in Copilot Chat to report the output.

What operational factors and settings allow for effective and responsible use of Copilot?

Copilot has been reviewed by our Responsible AI (RAI) team. We follow RAI principles and have implemented:

  • Responsible AI handling pipelines to mitigate the risks like harmful, inappropriate content.
  • In-product user feedback with which users can report offensive content back to Microsoft.
What should I do if I see unexpected or offensive output when using Copilot?
  • Use the thumbs-down button in Copilot Chat to report the output.
  • Remove or edit any inappropriate content before sharing.
  • Contact your IT administrator if you encounter persistent issues.
  • Your feedback helps Microsoft improve Copilot’s safety and quality.
Is the content generated original?

Content generated by Copilot is created by AI models that are trained over large datasets of presentations, internal and external data. However, outputs are synthesized from patterns in training data and may occasionally resemble existing content. Always review for originality and appropriateness before use.

How does image generation work in Copilot?

Copilot supports image generation using advanced AI models.

Request an image in chat, and Copilot will generate one if appropriate. Images can be inserted directly onto slides or returned in chat for manual placement depending on the request.

How does Copilot use my uploaded images in image generation?

When you upload an image or refer to one in a slide as a reference for generation, Copilot uses AI to analyze the entire image, including objects, background, and style. If people are present, the analysis may include visible physical and facial features, as well as the number of individuals. Based on your instructions, Copilot may stylize the image, modify the background, or add new elements. In some cases, it may recognize well-known public figures but otherwise can’t identify unique individuals.

Users must ensure they have the appropriate rights and permissions to use any uploaded images, including consent from all individuals depicted.

Where can I learn more about privacy?

Copilot and Microsoft 365 are built on Microsoft’s comprehensive approach to security, compliance, and privacy.

A few things to note

This feature uses advanced AI technology to generate content from your input. As with any evolving technology, outputs may vary and may not always be accurate or aligned with your intent, and may occasionally include sensitive content. We recommend reviewing and verifying AI-generated content before including it in your presentation. Similar inputs may produce similar results.

Elevate your presentation game with Copilot’s text rewrite feature in PowerPoint

Applies to: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365.

Copilot’s rewrite feature in PowerPoint can help you rephrase selected text based on length, tone, style, and more.

Note

If you don’t see Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or OneNote, it might not be included with your Microsoft 365 subscription or available based on your organization’s settings. Learn which Copilot license you have.

Using the PowerPoint Rewrite Feature

  • Select the textbox containing the text you want to rephrase.
  • Select the pen button that appears.
  • Choose one of the options: Custom prompt, Auto-rewrite, Condense, Make professional, or Visualize as a list.
    • Custom prompt: Tell Copilot in your own words how you want to revise your text. For example, you could say “Make this funny and easy to read.”
    • Auto-rewrite: Ideal for general improvements in grammar, spelling, and clarity.
    • Condense: Best for summarizing text while preserving the original tone.
    • Make professional: Suitable for making text sound more professional without changing its length.
    • Visualize as a list: Best for summarizing your paragraph in bullet points.
  • Review the suggested changes and select Keep it if you’re happy with them.
  • If you want Copilot to try again, select the Regenerate button.
  • If you want Copilot to try again with new instructions, write in the text box how you would like the text to be rewritten.

Frequently asked questions about Copilot in PowerPoint

Microsoft Copilot help & learning

Frequently asked questions about Copilot in PowerPoint

Applies to: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365, PowerPoint for iPad.

Copilot in PowerPoint can help you draft content, transform a Word file into a presentation, generate summaries, ask questions about a presentation, and get ideas about specific topics. Some of the frequently asked questions are below:

What are Copilot in PowerPoint’s intended uses?

  • Generate a presentation by asking Copilot what you want to write about, with no files referenced.
  • Generate a presentation based on the content of an existing Word document, with support for one file at a time. If you’re licensed with Microsoft Copilot, you can choose from Word or PDF—and encrypted documents are included as well.
  • Provide a summary of a presentation through a chat interface.
  • Provide answers to your questions based on the content in a presentation through a chat interface.
  • Create text content through a chat interface.

Why is the Copilot button in the ribbon grayed out, inactive, or not there?

Copilot in PowerPoint can only be used with PowerPoint files (.ppt, .pptx) and needs an internet connection.

Microsoft Copilot has specific requirements for app version, license, network, and privacy settings. If you don’t have Copilot available in the ribbon and you think you should have it, verify that you meet the Microsoft Copilot requirements.

What are the limitations of creating a presentation from a file?

If you have Copilot Pro (home), we support creating a presentation based off a single Word file, which can be referenced by typing “/” in the Copilot compose box and picking the file you want to use.

If you have Microsoft Copilot (work), you’ll also have the option to use a PDF, and encrypted files will be included. For more information, see Create a new presentation.

Also, Copilot is currently limited in the number of words it can process per prompt. For more information about processing longer files, see Keeping it short and sweet: a guide on the length of documents that you provide to Copilot.

What is the Rewrite feature in PowerPoint?

The Rewrite feature helps users improve and adapt their slide text with options like Auto-rewrite, Condense, and Make professional. It’s designed to help users fine-tune their text content to meet their presentation needs.

The Rewrite feature offers three pre-defined options:

  • Auto-rewrite: Improves the message by removing grammatical and spelling errors and bringing clarity in a neutral tone.
  • Condense: Reduces the length, removes grammatical and spelling errors, and maintains the original tone.
  • Make professional: Makes the tone professional, removes grammatical and spelling errors, and maintains the same length.

What are the limitations of the Rewrite feature?

The Rewrite feature works only on textboxes and not on shapes or other objects. It supports one response at a time and works on the entire textbox, not on partially selected text. Users must split textboxes to rewrite partial text. The output is AI-generated content and should be reviewed and edited accordingly

What is the Design Suggestions feature in PowerPoint?

Design Suggestions helps users create visually engaging slides by suggesting layouts, text, and images based on the content in their presentation. It analyzes existing slides and recommends new slides using AI, making it easier to refine ideas into polished slides quickly. Suggestions are AI-generated and should be reviewed before use.

What are the limitations of the Design Suggestions feature in PowerPoint?

The slide layouts, text, and images created by Design Suggestions are generated by AI and may occasionally be inaccurate, misleading, or irrelevant. In some cases, content may not align with the intent of your slide or could include inappropriate or offensive content. You should always review, edit, and verify any content generated by Design Suggestions before sharing it.

Currently, Design Suggestions only officially supports results of the locale “en-US”. While it may produce results in other languages, their quality can’t be guaranteed. You should always verify content not in en-US with a native speaker before sharing it.

Will Copilot use my company’s branding?

Using your organization’s branding is only available to users licensed with Microsoft Copilot.

You can use any PowerPoint presentation or template file with your corporate brand as a template. You can create a new presentation from your corporate template or save a copy of your presentation with your corporate branding to create a new presentation with Copilot.

To experience the best results with Copilot, follow the guidance at Use your organization’s branding with Copilot in PowerPoint. You may need help from your template creators and IT admin to modify corporate templates and publish them in your Organization Asset Library (OAL).

Does Copilot understand any languages other than English?

Many languages are supported in Copilot scenarios. The quality is expected to be highest in English, while in other languages, the quality is expected to be improved over time. More languages and locales will be added in the future. Find more information at Microsoft Copilot supported languages.

The suggestions from Copilot in PowerPoint are from AI, and we highly recommend users to review the suggestions before accepting them.

Can I use voice commands?

Yes. In Copilot in PowerPoint, use the microphone button to interact with Copilot using voice commands to ask questions, get summaries, or receive suggestions. You can interrupt audio responses if necessary, and Copilot will respond to your new input.

How was Copilot in PowerPoint evaluated?

Copilot in PowerPoint was evaluated through extensive manual and automatic testing on top of Microsoft internal usage and public data. More evaluation was performed over custom datasets for offensive and malicious prompts (user questions) and responses. In addition, Copilot in PowerPoint is continuously evaluated with user online feedback.

How is the Rewrite feature evaluated?

The feature is evaluated through a combination of comparative analysis, human review, automated testing, red teaming, and customer engagement metrics. User feedback and text kept rates gauge the effectiveness of generated text.

What operational factors and settings allow for effective and responsible use of Copilot in PowerPoint?

Copilot in PowerPoint has been reviewed by our Responsible AI (RAI) team. We follow RAI principles and have implemented:

  • Responsible AI handling pipeline to mitigate the risks, like harmful, inappropriate content.
  • In-product user feedback with which users can report offensive content back to Microsoft.
  • Data privacy and security: Implement robust data privacy measures to protect customer information.
  • User training and guidelines: Provide comprehensive training on the system’s features, capabilities, and limitations.
  • User permissions and access control: Implement role-based access control to limit functionalities and data access.
  • Monitoring and auditing: Regularly monitor system usage and conduct periodic audits.
  • Transparency and explainability: Clearly communicate how the system works and its limitations.
  • Accountability and error correction: Establish mechanisms for addressing errors and inaccuracies in system-generated content.

What should I do if I see unexpected or offensive output when using Copilot in PowerPoint?

Copilot in PowerPoint includes filters to block offensive language in the prompts and to avoid synthesizing suggestions in sensitive contexts. We continue to work on improving the filter system to more intelligently detect and remove offensive outputs. If you see offensive outputs including images, please submit feedback in PowerPoint using the thumbs up/thumbs down feedback in the Copilot UI so that we can improve our safeguards. Microsoft takes this challenge very seriously, and we are committed to addressing it.

Can I trust what Copilot in PowerPoint creates?

Copilot in PowerPoint gives you a head start in crafting your presentation, but the content it generates can be inaccurate or inappropriate. It can’t understand meaning or evaluate accuracy, so be sure to read over what it writes, and use your judgment.

While these features work to avoid sharing unexpected offensive content in results and take steps to prevent displaying potentially harmful topics, you may still see unexpected results. We’re constantly working to improve our technology to proactively address issues in line with our responsible AI principles.

As with any AI-generated content, it’s a great tool to get started, but it’s important that you review, edit, and verify anything it creates for you.

Is the content original?

Copilot in PowerPoint generates the content on slides based on language patterns it has found throughout the internet. Sometimes its results will be very similar to existing internet content, or Copilot might generate the same or very similar content for multiple people who are prompting Copilot in the same way.

For example, anyone who instructs Copilot to “add a slide about banana ice cream” is likely to wind up with identical or nearly identical content.

Where do the images come from?

Copilot in PowerPoint pulls images that are licensed for Microsoft within the PowerPoint context. To learn more about using these images, see What am I allowed to use premium creative content for?

Copilot in PowerPoint is also able to generate images using the content on slides.

For answers to frequently asked questions about suggested images from Copilot in PowerPoint, see Copilot in PowerPoint image suggestions FAQ.

Do I need a Microsoft Designer license to use Copilot in PowerPoint?

If users don’t have a Microsoft Designer license, they can access Copilot in PowerPoint features like summarization, open-ended Q&A prompting, and basic chat features.

However, some features only work if the user also has a Designer license. These features include adding a slide, creating a presentation about a specific topic, creating a presentation from a file, organizing the presentation, and adding an image to the presentation.

If you would like to use Copilot in PowerPoint for features that require a Designer license, talk to your organization’s IT admin about acquiring and enabling Designer licenses.

For information on the requirements for Designer on various operating systems, see Requirements for Design Suggestions for Windows.

Where can I learn more about the privacy of my data with Copilot?

Copilot and Microsoft 365 are built on Microsoft’s comprehensive approach to security, compliance, and privacy.

For more information about privacy, see the following information:

  • If you’re using Microsoft Copilot in your organization (with your work or school account), see Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot.
  • If you’re using Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps for home (with your personal Microsoft account), see Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps for home: your data and privacy.

Keep your presentation on-brand with Copilot

Applies to: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365.

Last updated: July 2026

Important

Copilot (including Brand kit) is available in PowerPoint for Windows, Mac and the web.

Your PowerPoint template is the foundation Copilot learns from. A well-structured template helps Copilot in PowerPoint generate on-brand, visually consistent presentations.

When you give Copilot in PowerPoint a prompt, it analyzes several sources to generate brand-consistent output:

  • Slides and layouts – The sample slide types and their layouts defined in your brand template.
  • Objects – Design elements like text, shapes, images and data visualizations in those sample slides, provided in templates.
  • Your prompt – The specific instructions you provide. Copilot synthesizes all this information to create slides that look like your organization created them. This is not just applying a theme – it’s understanding and replicating your brand’s presentation approach.

Note

If you don’t see Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or OneNote, it might not be included with your Microsoft 365 subscription or available based on your organization’s settings. Learn which Copilot license you have.

Optimize your PowerPoint templates for on-brand presentations with Copilot

Copilot primarily uses your sample slides, and secondarily your template’s structure and layouts to understand how your organization communicates visually. To generate presentations that reflect your brand, you can additionally set up a Brand kit which will apply your brand voice, tone, style and imagery, giving you results that reflect your brand’s look, layout, and content style.

This article explains how to optimize your PowerPoint templates so Copilot can produce more consistent, on‑brand presentations.

How Copilot uses templates to create presentations

Copilot in PowerPoint uses your:

  • Templates

  • Brand Kit assets to generate and edit slides using natural language prompts. When you ask Copilot to create or edit slides:

  • Copilot interprets your request.

  • It looks at sample slides and selects layouts from your template.

  • It generates content based on the template structure.

  • It applies brand assets like images, icons, and even brand voice from brand kits. Presentations created with Copilot prioritize your templates to produce on‑brand output.

Why template optimization matters

Copilot learns from:

  • Layout structure
  • Placeholder types
  • Content density
  • Visual hierarchy
  • Object relationships present in your template’s sample slides.

Without this information, Copilot may generate:

  • Generic layouts
  • Minimal formatting
  • Slides that do not match brand intent If your template does not contain enough sample slides, Copilot falls back to the Slide Master — which may result in less optimal output.

How to optimize your template for Copilot

1. Provide Representative Sample Slides

Copilot learns from the sample slides in your template. Therefore, your template should include representative slides that reflect how your organization typically presents content, so Copilot can extract and replicate those patterns to match your brand’s style. The more realistic and varied your samples, the better Copilot can understand and apply your brand’s presentation approach.

What to include in your sample slides

Ensure there are multiple slide types and layouts in your template. This helps Copilot recognize and reuse the right layouts.

We recommend adding the following generic layouts:

  • Title

  • Agenda

  • Section Header / Section Divider

  • Content (text, bullets, icons, focus areas, image layouts)

  • Data Visualization (tables, charts, statistics, dashboards)

  • Timelines

  • Process Diagrams (circular/block) / Flow Charts / Lists

  • Quotes / Statements / Testimonials

  • Questions and Answers (Q&A)

  • Summary / Key Takeaways

  • Conclusion

  • Thank You / Next Steps Scenario‑dependent or specialized slide types that also can be added are:

  • Introductions / Biographies

  • Team Slides / Meet the Team

  • Contacts

  • Maps

  • Calendar

  • Case Studies

  • Any other specific use case slide Note

These slide types are representative recommendations only and are not required. You may add any slide types based on your brand definitions and use cases; however, ensuring good coverage across layouts, slide types, and object styles will help produce better results.

Within those slides, show examples that demonstrate how your brand handles these concepts:

Content Density

Demonstrate how your brand handles varying amounts of information:

  • Light density: Titles/subtitles only, generous whitespace.
  • Medium density: Balanced layouts (e.g. text on one side and a large image on the other).
  • Heavy density: Content rich slides with minimal whitespace, including dense text, multicolumn layouts, and detailed charts or tables.
Visual Style

Show how visual elements are consistently applied:

  • Color usage across different slide types.
  • Color usage across different elements within graphs, charts, diagrams, etc.
  • Typography hierarchy, with examples of headings, subheadings, and body text in use.
  • Icon and image incorporation into layouts via placeholders or actual icons placement.
  • Multicolor variants of slide types, where appropriate (e.g. various section header slides in different colors).
Photography/Image styles

Include examples that reflect how your brand uses images in the slides. Use multiple slide examples to demonstrate:

  • Preferred composition and layout styles.
  • Image usage patterns (e.g. full bleed background images on title slides or inset images on content slides).
Data Visualization

Show how data is presented for your brand:

  • Layouts for highlighted statistics and key takeaways.
  • Examples of charts, tables, processes, timelines, diagrams, and infographics as they appear on slides for your brand.
Tips for best results
  • Design slide types with a clear, recognizable purpose. When each slide intent is obvious, Copilot can more effectively choose and use the right layout.
  • Create complete, end-to-end slide layouts that demonstrate a single, clear use case. Cohesive sample slides — rather than collections of individual elements like icon libraries or charts libraries — help Copilot better understand how the full slide layout is intended to be used, resulting in more consistent and polished presentations.
  • Keep your template focused on reusable layouts and place any instructional or guidance content outside the template.
  • Ensuring that negative spaces of objects, especially text boxes, do not overlap with other objects – this will help improve how Copilot reads and generates the output.
  • Choose layouts that reflect how you actually work day-to-day.
  • Use images and icons to improve readability and visual flow.

2. Set Up Your Template in Slide Master

Note

Customize your template in Slide Master to ensure consistent branding across all AI generated slides. With the ability to understand sample slides, Copilot uses Slide Masters only when there are not enough sample slides added.

To learn more about working in Slide Master view, see What is a slide master?

How to access Slide Master:

  • PowerPoint Desktop → View tab → Slide Master (in Master Views section)
Hierarchy:

There is a hierarchy of slides. The topmost slide is the Slide Master. Any elements or slide level definitions on the Slide Master will be inherited by the slides below it, known as Slide Layouts.

Important

You can use a PowerPoint template to create a presentation on any platform, but templates must be created in PowerPoint for Windows or Mac (not Web).

3. Use Theme Settings (Not Manual Styling)

Copilot learns from theme definitions, not one-off formatting.

Define Theme Colors
  • Go to Slide Master > Colors > Create New Theme Colors
Set Theme Fonts
  • Define heading and body fonts in the theme.
  • Use consistent font sizes and hierarchy.
Standardize Visual Styles

Apply consistent styles across all layouts:

  • Color schemes for charts and data visuals.
  • Icon styles.
  • Shape styles (rounded corners, borders, etc.).
  • Image placeholder styles.

4. Use Placeholders Correctly

Placeholders help Copilot understand content structure. Placeholders are defined containers for content such as:

  • Titles
  • Body text
  • Image
  • Chart
  • Table Copilot uses placeholder type, position, and size to determine what content should be generated and where it should appear. Copilot does not rely on placeholder text wording to understand layout intent.
Best practices
  • Use text placeholders instead of text boxes.
  • Insert placeholders by going to Slide Master > Insert Placeholder.
  • Keep placeholders readable and nonoverlapping with other objects.
  • Avoid placing decorative elements on top of text or image areas.

5. Upload your templates

Once your template is optimized, upload it to your Brand kit for Copilot to use. To upload to Brand kit, follow these steps:

  • Open the Microsoft Copilot app.
  • Select Create in the left navigation menu > More… > Brand kits.
  • Open your Brand kit.
  • Go to Templates.
  • Click Upload Template or select an existing template from your Organization Asset Library.
  • Select your .potx file or .pptx file.
  • Add metatags (optional).
  • Select Add to Brand kit.

How to use your Brand Kit assets in PowerPoint

After you complete setting up your Brand kit, you can select it in PowerPoint to generate on-brand content with Copilot.

  • Open your presentation in PowerPoint, then open the Copilot pane.
  • Select the + button in the Copilot pane.
  • Select Select brand.
  • Choose the Brand kit you want to use for the presentation.
  • Enter your prompt, then use Copilot to generate content that follows the selected Brand kit. After you select a Brand kit, Copilot uses that kit’s approved templates, colors, fonts, and assets to help keep generated slides aligned with your organization’s brand.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do we need sample slides for every layout?

No. Provide representative sample slides across typical and specific slide intents.

Will images be placed into picture placeholders reliably?

Yes. Copilot recognizes picture placeholders and places images in the appropriate position.

Can placeholder text be used as semantic guidance?

No. Placeholder text is used for styling only and is not treated as instructions.

What happens if generated text needs more space?

Copilot does not change the font size or placeholder size. It may instead add additional design elements to accommodate the content.

Are instructional slides allowed?

Instructional slides can remain if they follow reusable layouts, but mixing instructions with regular content may lead to unintended output.

What template formats are supported in Brand Kit?

Both .pptx and .potx are supported as template files.

Will Copilot follow the template if I open it first?

Yes.

Manage template settings in your Brand Kit for Copilot in PowerPoint

Applies to: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365.

Last Updated: Aug 2026

A Brand Kit stores the logos, templates, fonts, and colors that keep presentations on brand. As a brand manager, you can control how much freedom Copilot in PowerPoint has when it creates presentations from your branded templates. Two template settings give you that control:

  • Strict brand adherence (strict mode) — set for the whole Brand Kit. It controls whether Copilot can create new layouts or must reuse your approved ones.
  • Note instructions (note steering) — guide Copilot with plain-language instructions written directly in a slide’s notes. You can use either setting on its own or both together.

Important

Only the Brand Kit owner or brand manager can change these settings. End users who create presentations from your templates can’t override them.

Turn on strict brand adherence

Strict brand adherence restricts Copilot to your approved template and slide master layouts. When it’s on, Copilot won’t add or remove placeholders or invent new layouts. Use it when brand consistency matters more than creative flexibility—for official, customer-facing, or regulated presentations.

Setting

What Copilot does

On

Your template is always followed. Copilot uses only the template and slide master layouts and can’t add or remove placeholder content.

Off

Your template isn’t strictly followed. Copilot may reuse some template layouts or get more creative, while still applying your brand colors, fonts, and assets.

To turn strict mode on or off:

  • In your Brand Kit, open Manage Brand Kits.
  • Expand the Templates section. The header shows the current state, for example Strict mode: Off | 1 template.
  • Turn the Strict brand adherence toggle On or Off. A confirmation dialog appears—select Turn on (or Turn off) to confirm. Your change saves automatically and applies whenever the Brand Kit is selected—from the create-presentation template picker or the Brand Kit dimension in the Copilot pane.

Guide Copilot with note instructions

Note instructions (note steering) let you give Copilot per-slide guidance written directly in a slide’s speaker notes. Copilot reads those notes each time it creates a presentation from your template, so you don’t have to repeat the same preferences in every prompt—just embed the rule once. For example, “Always include this cover slide,” “Don’t modify this slide,” or “Keep the text on this slide minimal.”

Because the notes live inside your Brand Kit template, every presentation your team generates from it inherits the same guidance—giving you more predictable, on-brand output with less back-and-forth.

Step 1: Add steering instructions to the slide notes

Open your branded template. For each slide you want to control, open the speaker notes and type a plain-language instruction that describes how Copilot should treat that slide. Write the notes in clear, simple language—the same way you’d instruct a colleague.

Goal

Example note to add

Always keep a key slide

“Always include this cover slide.”

Protect a fixed slide

“Don’t modify this slide.”

Control text density

“Keep the text minimal.”

Enforce slide order

“Always include this slide last.”

Lock brand elements

“Do not change the logo, colors, or layout on this slide.”

Control visuals

“Always use a bar chart, not a pie chart.”

Set tone

“This slide is for an executive audience—keep it high-level.”

Step 2: Name and upload the template to your Brand Kit
  • Save your template with a clear, easy-to-identify name (for example, Notes steering – Company Toolkit). A consistent naming convention helps your team pick the right template later.
  • In your Brand Kit, open the Templates section and select Add template.
  • Upload your template. It appears in the Templates gallery, ready for your team to use. Once your notes are part of a template in your Brand Kit, Copilot uses them automatically—no extra setup is needed.

Note

When you upload a template to a Brand Kit, its note instructions are checked to make sure the content is appropriate.

Create a presentation that follows your Brand Kit

After your template is uploaded, anyone on your team can generate on-brand presentations that automatically follow your strict-mode and note-steering settings.

  • Open PowerPoint and open the Copilot pane.
  • In the prompt box, select the + button, and then select Select brand.
  • Choose the Brand Kit that contains your template.
  • Describe the presentation you want—for example, “Create a short presentation about our company history.”
  • Let Copilot generate the presentation. It applies your branded template and follows the instructions in the slide notes (for example, always including the cover slide).
  • Review that the output reflects your settings: the required slides are present, protected slides are unchanged, text density follows your rules, and any ordering or layout requirements are respected. To refine the behavior, update the notes in your template and upload it again.

Quick reference

  • Add plain-language instructions to the slide speaker notes in your template.
  • Name the template clearly and upload it to your Brand Kit under Templates.
  • (Optional) Turn on Strict brand adherence to keep Copilot to your approved layouts.
  • In the Copilot pane, select + > Select brand > your Brand Kit.
  • Prompt Copilot, generate the presentation, and review that your settings were applied.

Record a skill in Copilot in PowerPoint

Applies to: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365, PowerPoint for iPad.

Note

If you don’t see Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or OneNote, it might not be included with your Microsoft 365 subscription or available based on your organization’s settings. Learn which Copilot license you have.

If you repeat the same presentation-editing task, you can record it as a reusable custom skill. Copilot uses your changes in PowerPoint to draft the skill’s instructions and saves it to your personal Skills folder in OneDrive.

Record a skill

  • Open the presentation and the Copilot pane. In the prompt box, select +, and then select Choose skills. At the bottom of the list, select Manage plugins & skills.
  • Under Custom skills, select Add skill > Record Skill.
  • Recording starts automatically. Complete the presentation task you want to reuse. You can give Copilot instructions, edit slides directly, or use controls on the PowerPoint ribbon to update the slides.
  • When the task is complete and the intended changes appear in the presentation, select Stop.
  • Important
  • Wait for Copilot to finish any action and confirm that the changes appear in the presentation before you stop recording. An action still in progress might not be included in the skill.
  • Wait while Copilot processes the recorded actions and creates a skill draft.
  • Review the generated Name, Description, and Instructions. Edit the draft as needed, and then select Upload.
  • When the Skill uploaded confirmation appears, select Done. To capture another workflow, select Record again.

Use or manage a recorded skill

To use the skill, select + in the Copilot prompt box, select Choose skills, and then select the recorded skill. You can also use a skill by typing its name as an @mention in your prompt.

To manage custom skills, select Settings in the Copilot pane, select Manage plugins & skills, and then select Custom skills. You can turn a skill on or off, edit it, or delete it. A skill you turn off is not used automatically and does not appear in the skills menu. Custom skills are stored in your personal Skills folder in OneDrive.

Tips for recording a useful skill

  • Record one clear, repeatable outcome at a time.
  • Keep the recording shorter than 10 minutes.
  • You can experiment, make corrections, and use Undo or Redo. Copilot focuses on the main task and the resulting presentation changes.
  • Before you stop, verify that every change you want to reuse is visible in the presentation.
  • Good candidates include recurring slide formatting, table cleanup, chart styling, logo placement, layout changes, and regular presentation updates.

Known limitations

  • A recording must be shorter than 10 minutes.
  • Voice narration isn’t recorded.
  • Actions performed after switching to another application or window aren’t recorded.
  • A Copilot action that is still running when you stop might not be included.

Use connectors with Copilot in PowerPoint

Applies to: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365, PowerPoint for iPad.

Note

If you don’t see Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or OneNote, it might not be included with your Microsoft 365 subscription or available based on your organization’s settings. Learn which Copilot license you have.

Connectors let Copilot in PowerPoint use information from connected apps and data sources when helping you create or refine a presentation. After a connector is available and connected, you can ask Copilot to find relevant information and use it as context in your presentation workflow.

Connectors can help you bring useful information into PowerPoint without switching apps or manually copying and pasting content. You control which connectors are available for Copilot in PowerPoint to use, including data from external sources through federated connectors.

Enable or disable connectors

You can enable or disable connectors from the Copilot chat field.

  • In PowerPoint, open Copilot.
  • In the chat field, select the + button in the lower-left corner.
  • From the expanded menu, select Change data sources.
  • In the connectors list, review the connectors enabled by your admin.
  • Select Connect for a connector, or turn on a connector by using its toggle. Data sources that are turned off aren’t used by Copilot in PowerPoint. Depending on the connector and your organization’s settings, you might need to sign in or grant permission before Copilot can use that connector. If a connector is disabled or unavailable, contact your IT admin.

Admins can review connector availability and controls in Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors overview.

Federated connectors

Federated connectors are available to customers with a Microsoft 365 Copilot commercial subscription. Federated connectors let Copilot retrieve information directly from external services in real time without importing or storing that information in your presentation.

Copilot uses your credentials and only accesses data you have permission to view. You must give explicit consent before any data is sent to an external service.

After you approve a federated connector, Copilot can use it to answer questions and help create or update a presentation. Copilot’s response cites the sources it uses, so you know where information comes from. Your admin can also control which connectors are available in your organization.

To learn more, see Federated connectors in Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Available connectors

Available connectors may vary by tenant, license, and admin configuration. Examples include:

  • Moody’s: Connects to Moody’s credit intelligence platform to provide access to credit ratings, research, and risk insights.
  • CB Insights: Provides market insights, private company data, investment activity, and emerging trends.
  • Linear: Connects to Linear to surface and work with issues, projects, and roadmap data.
  • Notion: Connects to Notion workspaces so users can search, retrieve, and use content from pages, databases, and notes.
  • HubSpot: Connects to HubSpot CRM data so users can access customer, sales, and marketing insights.
  • Daloopa: Extracts structured, audit-ready financial data from company filings with traceability back to source documents.
  • FactSet: Provides access to financial datasets, market data, and analytical tools.
  • Intercom: Connects to Intercom customer communication data.
  • LSEG: Connects to LSEG’s financial data platform for market data, analytics, and valuation tools.
  • Morningstar: Provides investment research, analyst ratings, and market data.
  • PitchBook: Provides company, investor, and private-market transaction data.
  • S&P Global: Provides access to S&P Global datasets, including company financials and market intelligence.

Microsoft-built connectors

Use Microsoft-built connectors to integrate Copilot in PowerPoint with Microsoft services and external platforms. Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors let you access information across your organization’s platforms, such as work items, tickets, database rows, or CRM records, and then analyze them with Copilot in PowerPoint.

For more information and the full list of connectors, see the Microsoft-built connectors gallery.
